Breakthrough equation Y = f(X) + epsilon; principle of determinism (Figure 2-1)
Cause and effect; correlation vs causation; superstitious delusions; confounding variables
Variation happens: common-cause vs special-cause variation; short-term/long-term intro

DMAIC project strategy overview (Figure 3-1), five phases

formulas.name: Breakthrough equation

symbols.Y: the outcome, the result you desire or need
symbols.X: represents the inputs, factors, or pieces that are needed to create the outcome (can have several Xs)
symbols.f: the function, the way or process by which the inputs are transformed into the outcome
symbols.ε: the presence of error, the uncertainty in depending upon the Xs and the transformation function to actually create the desired outcome

formulas.conditions: Called the breakthrough equation. Book states: 'Everything is deterministic. All outcomes are a result of some process or function acting on the inputs.'

formulas.name: Mean

symbols.Σ: Greek capital letter sigma, sum up all the individual measurements
symbols.xᵢ: each of the individual measurement values
symbols.n: the number of individual measurements in your data set

formulas.conditions: For the purchase order example, n = 100 gives x̄ = 49.9 seconds.

formulas.name: Range
formulas.conditions: Simplest measure of spread; drawback is that it is greatly influenced by outliers.

formulas.name: Individual deviation score

symbols.xᵢ: any single recorded measurement from your set of data
symbols.x̄: the calculated mean of your collected observations

formulas.conditions: Acts as a numerical 'score' for each data point; negative when xᵢ is below the mean.

formulas.name: Squared deviation
formulas.conditions: Squaring penalizes points farther from the central location disproportionately more than those close (e.g., twice as far away scores four times worse).

formulas.name: Summed squared error (SSE)

symbols.Σ: add up all the individual squared scores

formulas.conditions: Statisticians call this result the summed squared error, or SSE for short.

formulas.name: Variance

symbols.n: the total number of data points you have collected

formulas.conditions: Divided by n−1 rather than n because using the mean (x̄) in the formula loses the independence of one of the collected measurements.

formulas.name: Standard deviation
formulas.conditions: Most commonly used measure of dispersion; units are the same as the original measurements.

formulas.name: Sequential range (short-term)
formulas.conditions: Only valid on a sequential set of measurements in the order they were taken.

symbols.R̄: the average range or difference between sequential points

formulas.name: Short-term standard deviation
formulas.conditions: Never calculate on anything other than a sequential set of measurements in original order.

formulas.name: Long-term standard deviation
formulas.conditions: Identical in form to the overall standard deviation formula (Table 5-3). Book states: 'The calculated short-term variation should always be less than or equal to the calculated long-term variation.'

formulas.name: Median position, odd n
formulas.expression: [(n+1)/2]th value in the rank ordered sequence

symbols.n: number of observed points in the data set (odd)

formulas.conditions: Used to find the median of a rank-ordered data set with an odd number of points.

formulas.name: Median position, even n
formulas.expression: average of [n/2]th and [(n/2)+1]th values in the rank order sequence

symbols.n: number of observed points in the data set (even)

formulas.conditions: Used to find the median of a rank-ordered data set with an even number of points.

formulas.name: Slope (rise over run)
formulas.conditions: Zero slope = horizontal/flat line; negative slope = line slopes down left to right; positive slope = line slopes up left to right. Used in main effects/scatter plots to compare strength of effect.

given.example_1: As a company, our accounts receivable performance for the finance invoicing area is not meeting the goal of 47 days sales outstanding. Overall this is causing cash flow and budget problems.
given.example_2: As a company our final process yield performance for the paint and polish area is not meeting the targeted 97 percent yield. Overall this is causing floor space, shipment, and resource problems.
given.example_3: As a company our on-time delivery performance for our healthcare products area is not meeting the scheduling and delivery cost requirements. Overall this is causing delivery issues and customer dissatisfaction problems.

stated_answers.example_1_cost: costing us as much as $4 million per year
stated_answers.example_2_cost: costing us as much as $900,000 per year
stated_answers.example_3_cost: costing us as much as $3 million in lost revenues and $1.5 million in expenses per year

given.poor_statement: Inventory levels are too high and must be reduced.

stated_answers.improved_statement: Inventory levels at the West Metro inventory storage process in Scottsdale are consuming space, taking up asset management time, and creating cash flow issues. Inventory levels are averaging 31.2 days, with a high of 45 days. These levels have exceeded the target of 25 days 95 percent of the time since January 2004. We could save $250,000 per year if we were at the targeted level.

given.poor_statement: Human Resources is taking too long to fill personnel requests.

stated_answers.improved_statement: Recruiting time for Software Engineers for the flight systems design department in San Jose is missing the goal of 70 days 91 percent of the time. The average time to fill a request is 155 days in the human resources employee recruitment process over the past 15 months. This is adding costs of $145,000 per month in overtime, contractor labor, and rework costs.

given.poor_statement: Our hospital has a problem with the amount of insurance claim forms submitted with errors to the insurance company.

stated_answers.improved_statement: Insurance claim forms originating at the Fremont North Memorial emergency department are causing a loss of revenue, excessive rework costs, and delayed payment to the hospital. Forty-five percent of the claim forms have errors, with an average of 2.3 defects per form. This problem has existed since claims processing was moved to Kansas City in June 2004. Billings could increase by $3.5 million per month, rework cost could be reduced by 50 percent, and an additional 1.3 percent of revenue could be recovered if errors were occurring less than 5 percent of the time. Achieving this level of performance would increase profits by $395,000 per year.

given.poor_statement: Reduce inventory levels as soon as possible.

stated_answers.improved_statement: Reduce raw material inventory levels from 31.2 days average to 23 days average with a maximum of 27 days by August 1, 2004. This project will save $235,000 per year for interest, space, and personnel in support of our corporate goal to improve asset management and ROI.

given.poor_statement: Improve how long it takes for human resources to fill personnel requests.

stated_answers.improved_statement: Reduce the software engineer recruiting time from an average of 155 days to 51 days, with an upper limit of 65 days. This will meet the current maximum goal of 70 days greater than 99 percent of the time. The new goal will be achieved by June 1, 2004. It will support our Employer of Choice goal and achieve an annualized savings of $145,000 per month.

given.poor_statement: Re-train employees to eliminate inaccurate claims forms.

stated_answers.improved_statement: Reduce the defects per form from 2.3 DPU to less than 0.1 DPU by September 15, 2004. This will increase revenue collection by $3.2 million per month resulting in an additional $25,000 profit per month at an 8 percent profit margin. This project supports the corporate goal to increase revenue by 15 percent per year.

conventions.topic: Definition of Six Sigma performance / DPMO
conventions.as_stated: Six Sigma performance is the statistical term for a process that produces fewer than 3.4 defects (or errors) per million opportunities for defects.

The sigma scale is a universal measure of how well a critical characteristic performs compared to its requirements. The higher the sigma score, the more capable the characteristic. ... Table 1-2 shows the sigma scale.
In Six Sigma, we call this concept of compounding defect risk rolled throughput yield, and we explain it mathematically in Chapter 6.

Notice that the mean (x̄) is included [in the variance formula]. This is where you lose the independence of one of your collected measurements. ... using the mean (x̄) reduces the number of independent measurements available to compute the variance.

conventions.topic: Short-term vs long-term variation / common cause vs special cause
conventions.as_stated: This natural level of variation is called the short-term variation of a process. Often, it is designated with a simple ST notation. ... the overall combination is called the long-term variation of the process. In many cases, it is written with a simple LT notation. ... Short-term variation is synonymous with common cause variation... Long-term variation is synonymous with special cause variation.

conventions.topic: Short-term variation must be <= long-term variation
conventions.as_stated: The calculated short-term variation should always be less than or equal to the calculated long-term variation.

Entitlement is the level of variation that is naturally built into a process. It is the amount of variation you can expect from a process under the best conditions — even when all the special causes are identified and eliminated. (Of course, you can see that this is just another name for short-term variation.)

Always consider a 70 percent improvement over baseline performance as one possible way to determine the target improvement in your objective statement. Such rates of improvement are defined as 'breakthrough' rates.

There are three types of savings categories possible for every Six Sigma project: hard, soft, and potential. Hard savings reduce expenses and result in a financial improvement. Soft savings are financial benefits that may occur as a result of a Six Sigma project but are not accountable as a direct result of the project... Potential savings are a form of hard savings, but require some action or decision to become realized.
If there are more than two Ys, there's a good chance that your project is too large in scope. You may have to break the project into two or more projects to be successful.

A Six Sigma Black Belt may implement as many as four such projects a year [historically advertised to return a bottom-line value of $150,000 or more]. ... The Green Belt implements about two projects per year that historically are advertised to return an average bottom-line value of $35,000.

Generally speaking, Belts have 20 percent responsibility for defining and managing improvement, while management has 80 percent. When it comes to implementation — the MAIC portion of the breakthrough strategy — these percentages are reversed.
